newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Dec 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

West Australian cricket captain Tom Moody's career has been revived four years after being dropped from the national side. Moody has been selected to play for Australia in the opening one-day matches against the West Indies this weekend, and while he said he was a little shocked, he acknowledged that as long as he was still playing first class cricket he was always up for selection. Page 22.

Athletics Australia executive director Neil King said yesterday he was prepared for AA to suffer a 25 per cent reduction in overall funding as the Australian Sports Commission announces the results of its post-Olympic review tomorrow. King said this would definitely affect team preparations for the Sydney Olympics. Page 22.

The Western Australian Institute of Sport announced yesterday Australia has lost its Olympic gold medal-winning gymnastics coach, Russian Andrei Rodionenko, to Canada. While Rodionenko has coached Australia's women's team for the past six years, WAIS exeutive director Wally Foreman has accused the Australian Gymnastics Federation of making Rodionenko's position untenable. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The West Indian cricket team has renewed its call for all-rounder Phil Simmons to rejoin the tour squad, as it falls to 0-2 down against Australia in the five-Test Frank Worrell Trophy series. West Indian captain Courtney Walsh yesterday confirmed rumours that team management had requested an extra player for the squad, and it is believed Walsh is particularly keen to call in the experienced Simmons, who is currently playing in domestic competition in South Africa. Page 44.

One of Australia's least-known fiery sportspeople is squash player Anthony Hill, who yesterday walked out of the Mahindra International tournament in Bombay after clashing with New Zealand referee Gavin Whyte. Hill's behaviour saw him breach the Professinal Squash Association's disciplinary rules for the second time in a fortnight and he may be automatically banned from the game. Page 43.

Melbourne Knights sweeper Josip Simunic, classed as one of Australia's most promising soccer talents, has finally announced he will no loner be eligible for selection with Australia, the country of his birth, and will now play for Croatia, the country of his parents' birth. It is believed Simunic was unhappy over his non-selection in the Australian team for Atlanta, and felt he had a better chance of playing in the 1998 World Cup with Croatia than he did with Australia. Page 43.
THE AGE

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor believes Australia has the psychological edge over the West Indies, as yesterday's Test win gave Australia its third Test win in a row against the tourists. Taylor believes that in comparison to 1995, Australia has he confidence to put enough pressure on the West Indian team to make them crack. Page C14.

Australian men's hockey coach Barry Dancer, the Australian Institute of Sport senior coach who is standing in until newly-appointed national coach Terry Walsh takes over next month, believes his team is poised to make a clean sweep of the three-Test men'shockey series in India, where it will compete against Spain, Pakistan, Germany, India and the Netherlands. Page C12.

United States PGA Tour officials will next week inspect Kingston Heath, Royal Melbourne and Metropolitan golf clubs in the lead up to the announcement next week that Australia will host the 1998 President's Cup. A further five courses are believed to hav been shortlisted as possible venues for the biennial teams event: Sydney's New South Wales, Royal Sydney, and the Australian, the Royal Canberra in Canberra, and Adelaide's Kooyonga. Page C12.
THE HERALD SUN

Victorian cricket Test opener Matthew Elliott was relieved at news yesterday that the injury suffered in a mid-wicket collision with Mark Waugh was confirmed as a slightly torn lateral cartilage in his right knee. The best case scenario will see Elliott able to resume play in time for the third Test to begin on Boxing Day in Melbourne. Page 86.

The Tasmanian Football League unveiled plans last Friday for a stadium to fit 30,000 people in Hobart, in the latest attempt to convince the Australian Football League Commission to award it a place in the national competition. Page 86.

World kilometres cycling champion Shane Kelly has been selected to race for Australia in the lucrative keirin series in Japan next year. Kelly's selection, which should prepare him well for next year's world titles in Perth, will see him join triple Commnwealth sprint champion Gary Neiwand in 10 weeks of racing that should substantially increase his bank balance. Page 81.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian rugby union halfback George Gregan has lost his position in the final match of Australia's tour of Europe to New South Wales' Sam Payne. Selectors have named a squad of 21 for the match against the Barbarians at Twickenham on Saturday, which te Wallabies must win to ensure an unbeaten 13-match tour. Page 78.

Malcolm Johnston, who, 17 years ago became well known as the jockey that rode champion horse Kingston Town, is on the comeback trail. Yesterday, at the Rosehill barrier trials, Johnston rode two-year-old Belching Way for Gosford trainer Bob Law and looked trim and well. Page 74.

Australian soccer player Tony Popovic will leave the Sydney United club, after signing a contract to be paid six times as much playing for Japanese club Hiroshima Sanfrecce. Popovic will play under former Australian coach Eddie Thompson. Page 72.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
